subject: chem
title: Organic Synthesis
subtitle: Multi-step synthesis, functional group interconversion and planning routes.
concept: Organic synthesis involves planning a series of reactions to convert a starting material to a target molecule, choosing appropriate reagents and conditions at each step.
Key transformations: alkene → halogenoalkane → alcohol → aldehyde/ketone → carboxylic acid → ester; nitrile → amine or carboxylic acid.
Purification and yield are important practical considerations.

notes.heading: Key Functional Group Interconversions
items: The most important transformations to know as a connected network: alkane → (UV/halogen) halogenoalkane; alkene → (HX) halogenoalkane; halogenoalkane → (NaOH aq) alcohol → (Cr₂O₇²⁻/H⁺, distil) aldehyde → (Cr₂O₇²⁻/H⁺, reflux) carboxylic acid; secondary alcohol → (Cr₂O₇²⁻/H⁺) ketone; halogenoalkane → (NaCN/ethanol) nitrile (+1C) → (LiAlH₄) amine or (HCl(aq) reflux) carboxylic acid.
For each step, always state: (i) reagent, (ii) conditions/solvent, (iii) type of reaction.

notes.heading: Multi-Step Synthesis and Retrosynthesis
items: Retrosynthetic analysis: work backwards from the target molecule. Identify the last bond formed or functional group introduced, then the step before that, and so on to a suitable starting material.
Key considerations: does the chain length need to change? (Use the nitrile route for +1C.) Does stereochemistry matter? Is the target chiral — can HCN addition give the needed enantiomer?
Atom economy and percentage yield apply to each step — multi-step syntheses accumulate losses.

notes.heading: Purification and Purity
items: Purification methods: distillation (for liquids with different boiling points), recrystallisation (for solids — dissolve in minimum hot solvent, cool slowly to get pure crystals), column chromatography.
Test for purity: sharp melting point at the expected value (impurities lower and broaden the melting point range). GC retention time or TLC Rf compared with a pure reference sample.

definitions.body: Working backwards from the target molecule to identify synthetic routes and starting materials.
(Actual moles of product / theoretical moles of product) × 100%.

workedExamples.q: Outline the conversion of bromoethane to ethylamine in two steps via a nitrile.

steps.text: CH₃CH₂Br + NaCN (ethanol) → CH₃CH₂CN + NaBr (nucleophilic substitution → propanenitrile).
CH₃CH₂CN + 4[H] (LiAlH₄, then H₂O) → CH₃CH₂CH₂NH₂ (propylamine) — reduction of nitrile.
This sequence extends the chain by one carbon AND introduces –NH₂.

mistakes: Losing track of carbon chain length — always count C atoms in reactant and product.
Using the wrong oxidation state conditions — distil for aldehyde, reflux for carboxylic acid.
Forgetting that NaCN increases the chain length by 1 carbon.
tips: Learn the 'ladder' of oxidation states: alkane → (UV/X₂) halogenoalkane → (NaOH aq) alcohol → (Cr₂O₇²⁻) aldehyde → carboxylic acid.
For each step: state (i) reagent, (ii) conditions/solvent, (iii) type of reaction.
A nitrile route: halogenoalkane → nitrile (+1C) → amine (LiAlH₄) OR carboxylic acid (HCl reflux or NaOH then acid).

flashcards.q: What reagent converts an aldehyde to a primary alcohol?
flashcards.a: NaBH₄ (sodium borohydride) in aqueous/ethanol — nucleophilic addition/reduction.

flashcards.q: How do you increase the carbon chain length by one carbon from a halogenoalkane?
flashcards.a: React with NaCN (in ethanol) → nitrile (RCN); the nitrile has one more carbon than the halogenoalkane.
Working backwards from the target molecule to identify the starting material and reagents for each step.

flashcards.q: What conditions convert a nitrile to a carboxylic acid?
flashcards.a: Reflux with HCl(aq) (or NaOH(aq), then acidify) → RCOOH + NH₄⁺ (or NH₃).

flashcards.q: How do you test purity of an organic solid?
flashcards.a: Measure the melting point: pure substance melts sharply at the expected temperature; impurities lower and broaden the melting point range.

flashcards.q: What is the reagent for converting a carboxylic acid to an ester without a catalyst?
flashcards.a: Use an acyl chloride + alcohol (no catalyst needed — faster than esterification with H₂SO₄).

questions.q: What reagents convert CH₃CH₂Br to CH₃CH₂OH?
questions.exp: Warm aqueous NaOH: nucleophilic substitution replacing Br⁻ with OH⁻ → alcohol.

questions.q: How would you convert ethanol to ethanoic acid in one step?
questions.exp: Refluxing ethanol with acidified K₂Cr₂O₇ oxidises first to ethanal, then further to ethanoic acid.

questions.q: A student wants to make butanenitrile from 1-bromopropane. What reagent is needed?
questions.exp: NaCN in ethanol: 1-bromopropane (3C) + CN⁻ → butanenitrile (4C) + Br⁻.

questions.q: Which sequence converts propan-1-ol to propan-1-amine?
opts: Oxidise to acid, then react with PCl₅, then NH₃
questions.exp: propan-1-ol → propanoic acid (reflux, Cr₂O₇²⁻) → propanoyl chloride (PCl₅) → propanamide (NH₃) → propylamine (LiAlH₄).

questions.q: What is % yield if 3.6 g of product is obtained when 6.0 g is theoretically possible?

recall: List four functional group interconversions you can perform starting from a halogenoalkane.
Describe how to extend a carbon chain by one using the nitrile route.
Calculate % yield from actual and theoretical masses.
Describe how to test the purity of an organic product.
